l.i: lor ) in rebus facundiam suam exercere malunt : præstare putavi, hæc vel Barbarè tractari ab aliquibus, quam prorsus à nemine. Iaculum illud Ciceronianum existimo, ne in me hæreat, sic posse repelli: nihil minus in animo mihi fuisse, quam meas hic cogitationes literis mandare: sed propositum, mentem, quoad liceret, Psalmorum (Reformatorum Theologorum juxta Scripturas in hisce controversiis præcipue sententiam) aperire. Hanc scio tanti esse piis, ut illatinæ dictionis fastidium, modo illam intueri clarius possint, haud gravatim sint toleraturi.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament below the text (a cartouche with scrollwork, flowers and a fruit cluster) is not text and is not transcribed. The faint text lower on the page, including "Reverendi" and the large letter with "A D-", appears to be show-through from the other side of the leaf, so it is left out. The "A D-" at the foot right is read as a gathering signature with some doubt; it may be "A 2" or similar. The first word "lor" is a fragment from the previous page's last line, which is why the paragraph is marked cont="true". No page number is printed on this page.
